      What do these words mean?
      Critical window
      The few weeks around flowering when the crop decides how many grains it will have. Stress here costs more yield than at any other time.
      Water stress
      1 means the roots found all the water the leaves wanted. Lower means the crop closed its pores and slowed growth.
      Nitrogen index
      1 means the crop has all the nitrogen it needs for its size. Lower means it is short.
      Vernalization
      Winter wheat needs weeks of cold before it will head. Sown too late or in a warm place, it stays leafy and never sets grain.
      Maturity
      Longer varieties use more of the season and can yield more, but risk frost before they finish or heat at flowering.

      Locations use rounded long-term climate averages and generic soil textures, not real weather records or mapped soils. Model parameters are placeholders and the weather is a synthetic annual cycle, so read the shapes and the timing effects, not the absolute yields. Seeding-rate and depth responses are placeholder shapes: the model has no soil crusting or poor seed-to-soil contact, so it rewards shallow seed more than real fields do. The best choice is the highest-yield combination on a coarse grid of sowing dates, varieties and nitrogen rates for the current weather year, preferring less nitrogen when yields are within 1%.
